key_insight: A brain-inspired analysis identifies a contiguous layer span whose weights can improve language-model reasoning while largely preserving existing mathematical competence.
engineering_relevance: Targeted weight grafting offers a way to transfer reasoning gains into instruction-tuned hosts without replacing the entire model.
method: Apply diffusion-map embedding to matched base and reasoning-trained models from three families.
Locate contiguous layer spans with localized changes in otherwise preserved gradient profiles.
Graft weights from these spans into instruction-tuned hosts and evaluate mathematical reasoning and retention.
evidence_signal: Across three model families, targeted grafts improved mathematical reasoning on average, with gains increasing with region overlap and better retention of previously solved problems than grafts elsewhere.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify gains or establish whether the identified spans generalize beyond the studied model families and evaluations.
paper_title: Transferring an analysis of human brain organization to language models
